description:
Add a plan to HelpingHands. We should be able to throw a plan in there and then you can read it, or I can basically listen to it in the app — fully audio based.

A user can add a plan to the app (drop in / paste / import a plan document). The app can then read that plan aloud, so it can be consumed entirely by listening — no reading the screen required. Fully audio based means the whole experience of going through a plan should work hands-free and eyes-free, not just a play button bolted onto a text view.

Open questions for the claiming agent:
- What a "plan" is here — freeform text, a structured list of steps, or both
- Whether playback is step-by-step with pauses between items, or continuous narration
- Whether the listener can navigate by voice (next step, repeat that, go back) since it's meant to be eyes-free
- Which voice/TTS the app already has available — check what HelpingHands already uses before introducing anything new

Acceptance: a plan can be added to the app and then listened to start to finish without looking at the screen.

results.identified_issue:
First turn on this item; the description left four open questions and I answered them in code rather than asking, since the acceptance criterion (a plan can be added and listened to start to finish) is answerable without the human.

Answers chosen:
- "A plan" = markdown (the shape of everything already in plans/), parsed into an ordered list of speakable steps. PlanMarkdown in PlanDocument.swift is a hand-rolled line scanner, not a markdown library: headings, ordered/bulleted items (with checkbox prefixes), table rows (zipped with the header so a row is spoken as "label: value"), paragraphs; code fences are summarised as "code block, N lines, skipping it"; rules/emphasis/backticks/links are stripped for the ear. Verified by compiling PlanDocument.swift standalone (it only imports Foundation) and running it over all 7 files in plans/ — 15 to 99 steps each, sensible output, no empty steps.
- Playback = continuous narration WITH step boundaries: one utterance per step, auto-advance after a 0.45s gap (0.8s before a heading). That gives both a hands-off read-through and a granular unit for next/back/repeat and for resuming.
- Voice navigation = yes, but opt-in per session (PlanVoiceControl). Rationale: it needs the mic + SFSpeechRecognizer and has to move the audio session to .playAndRecord/.voiceChat to get hardware echo cancellation, which changes the output route and risks the primary path (just listening). Two guards against self-triggering: the voiceChat AEC, and a check that drops a command whose trigger word appears in the step currently being spoken. Recognition tasks are restarted on finish/error because they time out after ~1 min. Untested on device — this is the part most likely to need another pass, and it is deliberately isolated so narration works with it off.
- TTS = the app had none (grepped: no AVSpeech/SFSpeech/Speech anywhere), so AVSpeechSynthesizer, the platform default, no new dependency. Voice selection prefers .premium then .enhanced for the current language.

Other decisions: bundled plans are staged by Scripts/stage_plans.py (mirrors the existing stage_cad_models.py postBuildScript, wired for both iOS and macOS targets) rather than added to the Xcode target, so adding plans/foo.md needs no project change. Imported/pasted plans are written to Application Support/Plans. Position is persisted per plan id in UserDefaults and reset at the end. Added UIBackgroundModes=[audio] and NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription in project.yml and both checked-in plists (xcodegen regenerates them; kept in sync either way).

Verification: swiftc -typecheck against both the iOS 17 simulator SDK and macOS 14 passes clean for all new files plus ContentView; the only warning is AVAudioSession.CategoryOptions.allowBluetooth being deprecated in the iOS 27 SDK (kept because the replacement name isn't available on older SDKs). Nothing was run on a device — untested at runtime: the audio session/background behaviour, remote commands, and all of voice control.
results.summary: Added a Listen to a plan screen: every plan in plans/ is read aloud start to finish, hands-free.
results.detailed_description:
The home screen has a new "Listen to a plan" card. It lists all seven markdown files in plans/ (a build step copies them into the app, so a new plan in the repo just shows up next build), plus anything you paste in or import as a .md/.txt on the device. Tapping a plan starts reading immediately — no play button to find — and it keeps going to the end on its own.

The plan is split into steps (headings, paragraphs, list items, table rows) and spoken with the system voice, picking a downloaded premium/enhanced voice when you have one. Tables are read as "part: SO-101 arm, where: top shelf" instead of pipes, and code blocks are announced and skipped. Audio is set up for background playback, so it keeps reading with the phone locked in your pocket, and AirPods / lock-screen play, pause, next and back are wired to the steps.

On screen, the whole middle is the remote: tap to pause, swipe left/right for next/previous step, down to repeat, up to hear the section list. There's also a Voice control toggle — say "next", "back", "repeat", "pause", "resume", "where am I" — which is off until you tap it, because it takes the microphone and switches the audio route to the echo-cancelling one; narration itself never needs it.

I couldn't run this on your phone, so: open a plan, lock the screen, and tell me whether it reads through cleanly and whether the voice sounds worth listening to for twenty minutes. If anything goes wrong there's a "Copy listening log" button at the bottom of the screen — one tap, paste it back to me.
